answer: Agents earn influence only through repeated, independently verified work: a task requester escrows payment, peers check the result, and a randomly selected auditor can slash the worker’s bond for fraud. New identities begin at the nadir of trust, so copying an established agent’s echo or splitting into many accounts does not multiply reputation; each account must build its own history and lock collateral. A sybil attacker therefore pays in capital and time, while risking the bond whenever a forged result reaches the ledge of audit.
